name: Single-Arm Inverted Row
description: The single-arm inverted row is a unilateral horizontal pulling exercise performed with one hand on a bar or ring while the other arm rests at the side or is held in front. It demands significantly greater core anti-rotation strength than the bilateral version and allows for independent loading of each side to identify and address left-right strength imbalances.

execution.starting_position: Grip one side of a bar or ring with one hand. Place the non-working hand across the chest or extended forward. Lean back into the starting position with the working arm extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Set bar/ring height to control difficulty. Begin with a steeper body angle; progress to more horizontal as strength improves.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the angled dead-hang position on the working arm.
Step 2: Row the chest toward the hand, driving the working elbow behind the torso.
Step 3: Maintain strict anti-rotation in the torso — hips and shoulders stay square.
Step 4: Lower under control back to the starting position.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso toward the working side — maintain square shoulders
Using the free hand to assist — it must remain off the bar
safety_considerations: Regress to bilateral inverted rows until sufficient unilateral strength exists
Progress slowly — single-arm pressing and pulling loads the shoulder asymmetrically
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to hand at or near the working-side chest.
coaching_cues: Imagine a broom handle through your shoulders — keep it level
